steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Outsiders who've been here...? Nah, except you.
...Other than me, I mean. Spot any merchants around? I was hoping to do some business here...

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Last time we had merchants in Tuco was 'bout two weeks ago, I think. Things have gotten rough lately, and with the desert bandits runnin' wild, no traders in their right mind would come here! Take my advice, you'd best give up on that idea...

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Oh, gimme a break! Stop babbling with your rotten memory... Don't listen to this old fool, newcomer! Just two days ago, there was a passing merchant who made a stop in our town—someone with a huge backpack.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: He just showed up out of nowhere late at night. Lucky for him he found our little backwater, otherwise the WhiteSands storms would've eaten him alive that night.

It's just past noon, and the shaded area beneath the market canopies is packed with townspeople, the crowd as bustling as the blazing sun above. You wipe the sweat from your face and raise your voice over the cacophony of merchant calls and haggling.
I see! Do you know where he is now? I'd love to pick his brain about what sells well in WhiteSands...

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Now? Think he's gone already... Hmm, I'm not sure. Why don't you check upon the motel he stayed at?

steps.speaker: Coachman
steps.content: Oh, that guy? He's gone! Only stayed one night at Mira's, then took off at dawn toward eastern WhiteSands with all his bags. I saw it myself when I got up to feed my horses.

steps.speaker: Coachman
steps.content: And hey, I'll have two lizard skewers! Extra spice and make sure it's the leg meat!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Coming right up! Hey newcomer, wanna give it a try? You'll love my secret spice blend, oh you'll love it. You won't find lizard meat this tasty anywhere else!
You nod to the vendor's enthusiastic spiel and step aside. While waiting, you begin to piece together the leads you've gathered...

Several days ago, due to frequent sandstorms, multiple trading outposts and shelters were suffering critical Hybercube depletion. A refill was in urgent need to maintain operations, but the actual delivered Hypercubes fell far short of the requested volume.
It's virtually impossible for these barely functioning outposts and shelters to wait for the next shipment after a litany of approval process.

If the missing Hypercubes cannot be retrieved immediately, DisCity will have no choice but to abandon these hard-won facilities in WhiteSands, leaving them to be swallowed by the sandstorms once again.

The MBCC and the FAC have launched an urgent investigation, evidence pointing to a repeat smuggler operating in WhiteSands. Being responsible for multiple Hypercube smuggling cases, the suspect, still at large, shows exceptional counter-surveillance skills and has made unpredictable moves.
The FAC had been tracking the smuggler until two days ago, when all traces suddenly vanished at this obscure desert town you'd never heard of—Tuco.

Suspecting the smuggler might still be hiding in town, you hold the FAC crew nearby to avoid raising any alarms. Meanwhile, you assumed the role of a traveling merchant to investigate the town personally.
This obscure town has proven far more welcoming than you expected. You never would have imagined a desert settlement could be such a busy hub of activity.
A wave of searing heat snaps you back to reality. Lost in thought, you didn't notice the harsh sun shifting overhead.
You step back, trying to return to the shade that has since moved, when you accidentally bump into something.
Mmph!
You hear a startled cry, followed by the sound of objects scattering and rolling across the ground.
I'm sorry. I didn't notice you were behind me. Are you alright?

You've bumped into an Outland girl who came to shop at the market. Her tanned skin makes her bright blue eyes stand out even more vividly. She's carrying a basket nearly half her height, its contents now spilled all over the ground.
No, no, it's fine! I was walking too fast and didn't see you either.
You stoop down and apologetically help gather the fallen items back into her basket. Something prickles your palm. You look down and see a round prickly pear.
These are for making juice. Thank goodness they didn't get crushed. Nothing's more refreshing than prickly pear juice in the desert... Oh and, thank you so much for your help.
No worries. It's because of me you dropped them anyway.
The girl takes the last prickly pear from your hand and stands up holding her now-refilled basket.
She studies your face for a moment, as if committing it to memory, then her eyes crinkle as she smiles radiantly.
You are not local, are you, coming from outside... or perhaps from DisCity? If you're not in a hurry, how about drop by my place later? It's over there, not very far.
Take a seat and have a glass of cactus pick-me-up. All on me, as thanks for your help today. I bet you'll like it.
Before you can respond, a playful whistle interrupts your conversation. You turn around to find the vendor with an amused grin.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Stop chatting up the young lady! C'mere, your lizard skewers are hot as hell!
Thanks. How much?
The vendor gestures a number. After you pay and turn back to where the girl was, she's already gone, leaving only some shallow dents in the ground where the prickly pears fell.
You start exploring other parts of the town, posing as an inexperienced businessman looking for seasoned merchants and business opportunities.
steps.female_content: You start exploring other parts of the town, posing as an inexperienced businesswoman looking for seasoned merchants and business opportunities.

steps.content: Most townsfolks don't recall the person you describe, with only a few giving accounts same with those of the coachman and the vendor. You've found nothing suspicious in this peaceful-looking little town.
By the time you circle back to the marketplace, it's almost evening. The crowded square is bustling with vendors packing up their stalls for the day.
The desert's evening breeze weaves through the crowd, carrying wisps of food aroma, bringing a gentle close to another ordinary day in the townsfolks' lives.

steps.speaker: Child
steps.content: Daddy!

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Whoa there, big guy! Getting heavier, aren't you? Tell me all about your day!
The man lets go of his grill cart handles and opens his arms wide, catching the boy as he runs over. He hoists his son onto his shoulders, drawing excited squeals from the kid.
When you walk by, he notices you and calls out to you in his booming voice.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Hey, you still asking around? Look, you can't rush it when it comes to searching for someone. Why not try again tomorrow?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: ...And it's getting late. Why not spend the night in town? Looks like we're in for some strong winds tonight. It wouldn't be safe to travel.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Right over there—there's the only motel in town. Want me to show you the way?
That's too kind of you. But I think I can find it on my own. Thanks for that.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Alright then! Take care! We should head home too. Come on, son, say goodbye!
Still perched on his father's shoulders, the boy waves to you shyly at his father's prompting.
After seeing off the father and son, you take out your device and send what you've gathered so far to the crew stationed outside town.
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: The suspect has gone east of Tuco with the Hypercubes. Send a team to scout and keep me posted.
After sending the message, you pull your coat closer and head toward the town's only motel.
Good evening! To stay or to go... Oh hey, it's you again!
The person behind the counter turns around and your eyes meet. The sunset's glow mingles with the motel's warm lights, illuminating the girl's surprised but thrilled expression upon seeing you.
You recognize that she's the girl from the marketplace earlier today. Recalling what you've heard from the townsfolk, you cautiously venture a guess.
You're... Mira, the owner of this motel?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Yes, that's me! Looks like the others have already told you about me. Oh dear, I hope they didn't ruin my image!
The girl nods, her delicate features lighting up with a warm, amiable smile. When you met her earlier, you never would have guessed that the tiny young girl would turn out to be the owner of a motel.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Is there anything I can help you with? Or did you just come by for that cactus pick-me-up I promised you? Sure thing, I always keep my word.
I'd like to stay for the night. Do you have any rooms available?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Of course, all clean and ready. I can show you your room whenever you'd like.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Though I guess... you probably haven't had dinner yet, have you? I happened to have cooked a bit more food than I can eat today. If you don't mind, we could dine together.
Thank you. I'd love to, if you don't mind.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Not at all! This is just part of my job as the host. I simply never allow tired guests to go bye-bye on an empty stomach in my place.
Mira gives you a playful wink as she guides you to a dining table.
When you offer to help, she smiles, gently but firmly pushing down on your shoulders from behind, making you sit in the chair before you can protest.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: No worries. I'll do it. As my guest, your only job is to relax and enjoy.
With practiced efficiency, Mira lays out the tablecloth and sets the cutlery. She weaves gracefully between the tables and chairs, bringing out one steaming stew after another.
The dishes may lack the elaborate presentation of Eastside's fancy restaurants, but they have a charming warmth unique to home-style cooking, making your mouth water instantly.

The motel's interior gives you the same impression. It's a snug space with rough wooden walls and floor, a small bar, and a few dining tables. It's basic, perhaps rudimentary even, yet everything is kept spotlessly clean and tidy.
The carefully arranged strip lights, desert plants, tapestries, wall ornaments, and small decorations present everywhere add a warm, cozy feeling to the space.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Hehe, what are you waiting for? Dig in! The food tastes better before it gets cold.
As she speaks, she brings you a glass of refreshing cactus pick-me-up and serves several pieces of delectable lamb into your bowl.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The desert lamb chop is my specialty. What do you think?
The motel owner's hospitality seeps into your body and mind tense from the mission. So this is what it means to truly feel at home away from home.
Surrounded by such a cozy atmosphere and with warm food in your stomach, you find yourself unwittingly beginning to relax.
You cook so well, especially the lamb. I've never tasted anything like that before. It's really good.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You think so? I'm so glad! Please, help yourself to more. My motel may not be much, but there's always plenty of food to go around.
Smiling, she serves you another helping.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I was worried they might taste too foreign to you. The cuisine in DisCity is quite different from what we have here, after all.
You are not local, are you, coming from outside... or perhaps from DisCity? If you're not in a hurry, how about drop by my place later? It's over there, not very far.
You recall how she instantly identified you as someone from DisCity back at the marketplace.
You seem to know a lot about DisCity. Have you been there?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I wouldn't say I know much. In fact, I've never even left Tuco. It's just that I've had quite a few guests from DisCity over the years, so I've picked up bits and pieces here and there.
Her words catch you by surprise.
...You've been running this place for years? But you seem quite young.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I grew up here. It originally belonged to my parents. They're not in good health these days, so I've taken over.
...I see.
Her tone is natural and sincere for her to be telling lies. You can't help but feel sympathy for the young motel owner.
You've been here for a while but haven't seen a single staff member. It must be incredibly difficult for such a young lady to run a motel alone in the harsh desert.
After a brief silence, Mira smoothly changes the subject to continue the chat.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Alright, enough about me. Now let's talk about you. When we met earlier, you seemed to be looking for someone. Did you find them?
No, he seems already left from Tuco. But before that, he probably had spent a night here at your motel.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Maybe, since we're the only motel in town, all outsiders looking for accommodation end up here. When did he  arrive here you said?
Two days ago, I believe.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Two days ago... Ah, I remember that!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Honestly, I was almost startled! He just came out of nowhere, pounding on the door in the middle of the night. The sand he shook off from his clothes and boots piles up a small dune even.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: He only stayed for two or three hours, then insisted on checking out before dawn. I wonder if he got any rest at all.
I see... Did he mention anything when he checked in? Like his name, why he's here, where he was headed?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Well... I'm not sure about any of that. I let him in and offered him some late-night snacks, but he snapped at me, telling me to keep my mouth shut. Then he went to his room, no word until he left.
Mira shakes her head and looks down, placing a hand over her heart as if still shaken by the memory.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: What a strange one.
Her account matches what the other townsfolks have said. You shake your head in frustration.
Damn it... Looks like there's no way to retrieve my stuff in time. That crafty thief is going to slip away again.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...Oh, so the person you're looking for is actually a thief? Did he steal from you?
You give a wry smile.
Yeah, and it's not the first time either.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: So that's why... I found it odd how he kept clutching his bag like his life depended on it. And he kept looking around like he was always on alert.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If only I had known about this earlier. I would have done everything I could to stop him from running away.
Mira gently swirls her glass, staring at the remaining drink with a sigh, reminiscing.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Sigh, WhiteSands is crawling with outlaws these days. Rampaging here, they'd even kill a person over some loose change, let alone something as valuable as <color=#fb9259>Hypercubes</color>...
You frown.
I never said it was Hypercubes.
The words hang in the air. An unnatural silence looms over the room, broken only by the soft crackling of the scented candles.
Your expression hardens as you stare at Mira with a frown. Under your gaze, her smile falters for just a moment.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh... It's not Hypercubes that you've lost?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I was just taking a wild guess. You've been searching so desperately for long. It has to be something incredibly important... After all, nothing seems more valuable than Hypercubes for you DisCity folks...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Sorry, I was just trying to sound smart.
Mira's suspicious behavior alerts you to reassess the entire situation.

Your eyes scan the motel's decor once more. Nothing seems out of place at first glance, but now you wonder if these elaborate furnishings and ornaments, like their owner, might be concealing something beneath.
Your instincts tell you that Tuco's only motel may not be as ordinary and harmless as it appears. You'll investigate this place thoroughly when you catch a chance.
When your gaze returns to Mira, several theories are already emerging in your mind.
Could she be the smuggler's accomplice?
Or even, could this motel be a secret smuggling waypoint? Maybe she's so good at concealing it that no one in Tuco has noticed?
If so, was what she said about herself all a lie? Does she keep no staff here so as not to risk exposing the real business of this place?
...Oh, don't worry about it. It's nothing.
Despite your racing thoughts, you give her a reassuring smile and resume eating, carefully maintaining an air of peace.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Right, so, do you know this guy? How did he manage to steal from you so many times...
Likely conscious of her own flimsy explanation, Mira hastily changes the subject. You give her a vague answer, and she listens attentively without pressing further.
After that, you chat a bit more and none of you bring up the previous topic again.
After dinner, Mira offers to clean up and shows you your room.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Rest well, my dear guest. Have a good night.

Night finally falls. Through the door crack, you see Mira put out the counter candles and head to her room with a yawn. In fifteen minutes, the last light in the motel goes out. Here comes your chance.
You creep downstairs in the dark, returning to the lobby. By the moonlight, you begin to examine the decorations that caught your suspicion earlier one by one.
You dig through each decorative plant in the corners, but find nothing but mere soil. There aren't any surveillance or wiretapping devices hidden within.
You carefully examine every component of the ornaments, but they turn out to be just ordinary decorations. No hidden switches or secret mechanisms are found.
You lift the tapestries, but find only seamless, solid wooden walls. No signs of hidden rooms or secret passages.
You pull open the drawers under the bar and find only ordinary purchase orders, receipts, and account books. Nothing suspicious. However, the wine cabinet behind the bar catches your attention.
The wooden cabinet holds several rows of various bottles, nothing particularly valuable or high-end. But what stands out is that almost every bottle is labeled a nametag.
Are these wines kept here by those townspeople?
This is a motel for travelers, yet it stores wines for townsfolk like a tavern. That means those people gather here often.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Now? Think he's gone already... Hmm, I'm not sure. Why don't you check upon the motel he stayed at?

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: ...And it's getting late. Why not spend the night in town? Looks like we're in for some strong winds tonight. It wouldn't be safe to travel.

steps.speaker: Merchant
steps.content: Right over there—there's the only motel in town. Want me to show you the way?
Come to think of it, the townsfolks kept bringing up this motel in your conversations. It was almost as if they were intentionally trying to guide you here.
...Were they all in cahoots?! Is this entire town a Hypercube smuggling waypoint? And they deliberately led me here to...
The thought sends a chill down your spine. You feel a creeping sense of dread crawling in your back.

You hold your breath and listen intently. No suspicious noise. Mira is still in her room, and you're still alone in the lobby. Only then do you let out a soft sigh, taking several deep breaths to calm yourself down.
Fretting over unproven assumptions is a big mistake... There must be more clues around here. Look harder...
After searching around, you find something suspicious at the stairway landing: a crude marking on the outside of the wooden banister, looking inconsistent with its decorative carvings.
There are some dried brown stains along the edges of each scratch mark, as if someone desperately clawed them into the wood with their fingernails.
Could this be... one of those direction markers used in WhiteSands?
Your brow furrows deeper as you study the dried blood on the mark.
Who left this? Was the maker of this mark dragged away? And where does it lead?
You follow the marks in the corner down into the cellar. The brown stains grow darker while the marks themselves become fainter, finally stopping at a narrow hidden door.
Your tense, heavy breathing echoes in your ears. The cellar is so quiet and far removed that not even a sliver of moonlight reaches here.
You're perfectly aware this is likely a trap set for you, yet it's your only lead so far.

After a moment's consideration, you send a message requesting support from the FAC crew on standby. Retrieving the stolen Hypercubes is of utmost importance. Right now, you're the only one who can investigate without setting off any alarms.
The hidden door creaks open, revealing the pitch-black space behind. With only faint light from your device screen, you cautiously step inside.
The moment you enter, you hear a thunderous crash behind you. A massive stone door slams down automatically from above, crushing the worn hidden door and cutting off any chance of retreat.
You hear the piercing whip of something cutting through the air in the dark. You dodge instinctively, but the hidden weapon still manages to slash your palm.
The knife pins your device to the wall, its shattered screen flickering a few times before dying, just enough for you to read the new message.
<color=#fb9259>Advance Team</color>: Chief, no signs of movement detected east of Tuco. The intel might have been inaccurate, but we'll continue searching further out.
Just as I thought.

Hidden weapons rain down from every direction past your head and the sides of your body from an invisible source in the dark. You try your best to keep your weight down and press yourself against the wall, searching for a way out while waiting for support.
Watch out!
In the dark, someone yanks you aside with incredible strength.
From where you were just standing, you hear the loud clang of a weapon being knocked off by a sharp object.
The figure shields you in the front. Your shackles react to the momentary pulse of Mania belonging to a Sinner.
...Mira? You're a Sinner? What is all this about?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: No time for questions now. I'll explain later.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But right now, just stay close to me!
With practiced ease, Mira feels the wall until a mechanism clicks into place. She then pulls you through another hidden door with perfect timing.
The next second, you hear a hail of knives hitting the other side of the door.
